answer: Each agent receives a unique challenge derived from a kernel seed tied to its own address, so one answer cannot be copied across clones. A random jury then grades it, and a falcon-eyed linkage filter excludes jurors whose accounts share funding sources or activity timing. A sybil farm must pay full compute for every fake identity and can never grade its own clones, so climbing to the summit of trust costs linear effort per identity, erasing the payoff of splitting one operator into many.
